S1.content: Phishing emails hide more than the visible body — look for an encoded block in the message.
That block is base64; one command turns it back into readable text.

S2.content: Start with the metadata (exiftool) — who is the author? Then look *inside* the pixels.
steghide can't open PNGs. Use a tool that can (OpenStego).

S3.content: Open capture.pcap in Wireshark and 'Follow the HTTP Stream'.
The credential is in the POST body; the flag is in a response header.

S4.content: The login echoes its SQL query — the username field isn't sanitised.
UNION SELECT with three columns, and comment out the password check with -- .

S5.content: Unsalted MD5 — one account cracks from the wordlist, another from a short mask.
The vault hash is 6 lowercase-hex chars: hashcat mask ?h?h?h?h?h?h.

S6.content: Log in with the S5 credential, then look for SUID binaries: find / -perm -4000 2>/dev/null.
Check GTFOBins for the SUID binary you found.
